faq.q: When is the best time for dolphin watching in Cabopino?
faq.a: The peak dolphin watching season in Cabopino runs from June to September, with July and August offering the highest sighting rates. Early morning (09:00–11:00) and late afternoon (16:00–18:00) are the best times, as dolphins feed near the surface when the sea is calm and the sun is low.

faq.q: What types of dolphins can I see off Cabopino?
faq.a: The most common species are bottlenose dolphins and common dolphins. Bottlenose dolphins are larger and often travel in pods of 10–20, while common dolphins are smaller and more acrobatic. You may also spot striped dolphins or pilot whales during summer months.

data.body_html:
Cabopino, a charming marina just east of Marbella, is one of the Costa del Sol's best spots for dolphin watching. With its calm waters and rich marine life, the area offers excellent opportunities to see bottlenose and common dolphins in their natural habitat. If you're planning a Marbella boat rental for the 2049 season, timing is everything. This guide covers the best months, optimal departure times, and the ideal boats from our Puerto Banús fleet to maximise your chances of an unforgettable encounter.

Why Cabopino for Dolphin Watching?

Cabopino's position between Marbella and Estepona places it near the nutrient-rich waters of the Alboran Sea. This area attracts dolphins, sea turtles, and even migrating whales. The marina itself is quieter than Puerto Banús, making it a peaceful base. However, all our charters depart from Puerto Banús, just 15 minutes away by car. The short transit means more time on the water searching for dolphins.

Peak Dolphin Watching Season 2049

The dolphin watching season in Cabopino peaks from June to September. Water temperatures reach 22–26°C, and daylight hours are longest. July and August offer the highest sighting rates, with calm seas and consistent dolphin activity. May and October can also be good, but sightings are less predictable. For the best experience, book a charter between 09:00 and 11:00 or 16:00 and 18:00, when dolphins feed near the surface.

Best Boats for Dolphin Watching

Our fleet includes several vessels ideal for dolphin watching. For small groups of up to 11 people, the Azimut 39 (12.5m) is a popular choice at €749 for 2 hours. It offers a comfortable cabin and plenty of deck space. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m) accommodates 12 guests and includes a free jet ski, starting at €4,719 for 4 hours. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is another excellent option for intimate outings.

What to Expect on Your Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and safety equipment. You'll enjoy complimentary water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. Spanish IVA (21%) is included in the price. Your skipper will navigate to known dolphin hotspots off Cabopino, often near the Cabopino dunes or the Cala del Faro area. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a camera—dolphins can appear suddenly.

Combining Dolphin Watching with Other Activities

Many charters allow time for swimming or snorkelling at nearby coves like Cala Cortés or Cala del Faro. If you book the Mangusta 80, you can use the included jet ski to explore the coastline. For a full day, consider an 8-hour charter on the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Ferretti 94 (pricing on request). These longer trips can include a stop at Estepona or Sotogrande for lunch.

Booking Tips for 2049

Summer slots fill quickly, especially in July and August. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance. For the best value, choose a 2-hour Tier A charter (€749) for a focused dolphin watching experience. If you want a longer day on the water, the 8-hour Tier A charter (€2,299) offers flexibility. For luxury options, contact us via WhatsApp for pricing on boats like the Canados 86 or Maiora 26m.
